item.title: Let There Be Rock: Late AC/DC Frontman Bon Scott Remembered With Melbourne Mural
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to this special edition of our podcast, where we're celebrating the life and legacy of the one and only Bon Scott, the iconic frontman of AC/DC. As we speak, a brand new mural of Bon Scott has just been unveiled in Central Melbourne, ahead of what would have been his 80th birthday.
[Short music transition]
Host: The stunning artwork, created by Melbourne artist Era, is based on a design by Mambo artist and Mental As Anything co-founder Reg Mombassa. It's a fitting tribute to Bon's Celtic roots, which are also remembered with a lifesize statue in Kirriemuir, Scotland, where he was born.
[Short music transition]
Host: Bon Scott's music career was marked by his powerful pipes and bad boy attitude, fronting several bands before joining AC/DC. He performed on the band's first seven studio albums, including the legendary "Highway to Hell". Unfortunately, his life was cut short when he passed away in 1980 at the age of 33.
[Short music transition]
Host: But Bon's legacy lives on, and AC/DC has continued to salute him at every concert. The band was inducted into the ARIA Hall of Fame in 1988 and the Rock And Roll Hall of Fame in 2003. And now, this new mural in AC/DC Lane is a permanent reminder of his impact on Australian rock music.
[Short music transition]
Host: As Melbourne Lord Mayor Nicholas Reece said at the unveiling, "Melbourne is the undisputed home of live music in Australia, and AC/DC is part of our city's DNA." The mural is a must-see for any fan, and you can even take a piece of it home with you - exclusive Reg Mombassa x Bon Scott 80 merch is available online.
[Outro music plays]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to this special tribute to Bon Scott. His life and career may be gone, but they'll never be forgotten. Until next time, rock on!
